name: NoticeBench 65 — Prop 65 Sixty-Day Notice Response System
one_line: A single self-contained local .html (plus PDF playbook) that a company just named in a California Prop 65 60-day notice opens to see what materially identical past cases actually settled for — every benchmark record hyperlinked to the AG-hosted settlement PDF — whether the noticed chemical has a safe-harbor level and at what value, a dossier on the specific noticing party's settlement pattern, and a generator that emits the exactly-compliant warning text (2025 short-form amendment) for every sales channel.
buyer: Owner / compliance lead / non-specialist GC at US consumer-product SMBs and Amazon-channel brands named as 'alleged violators' — supplements, food, cookware, apparel, jewelry, hardware. Almost all USA (CAN-SPAM opt-out, legal). The person opening the scary letter can card $597 the same day; a defense firm quote starts at $10-25k.
trigger: The company's name appears as an alleged violator in a dated 60-day notice in the California AG's public database, which starts a statutory 60-day clock before a private enforcer may file suit. Notices show AG number, date filed, noticing party, plaintiff attorney, alleged violators, chemical, and product source, with per-notice PDFs. [VERIFIED — fetched live, HTTP 200, no login; data current through 2026-08-06 with e.g. Calvin Klein/Ross (PFOA), Amazon.com/Everyday Dose (lead), Siete Family Foods/Walmart (lead)]. Free CSV export up to 1,000 records per pull.
trigger_url: https://oag.ca.gov/prop65/60-Day-Notice-Search-Results — fetched directly, HTTP 200. Parent portal https://oag.ca.gov/prop65 also fetched (confirms 60-Day Notice Search + Annual Settlement Reports sections).
list_size: 5,398 notices filed in 2024 [PLAUSIBLE — realestatelanduseandenvironmentallaw.com year-end review]; monthly runs of 358-539 through 2024-2025 [PLAUSIBLE — Intertek monthly bulletins]; many notices name 2+ violators (brand + retailer), so named-company events exceed notice count. Call it ~5,000-6,000 named, dated companies/year, enumerable free with CSV export [database itself VERIFIED]. Roughly 2x DeckProof's ~2,400/yr, and it replenishes daily rather than per published roster.
corpus: Four assembled layers, all one-time work: (1) settlement benchmark dataset parsed from ~10 years of AG Annual Settlement Reports plus thousands of per-case settlement PDFs hosted at oag.ca.gov/system/files/prop65/settlements/ [VERIFIED paths exist; 2023: 797 settlements, $18.9M total, 88% to plaintiff attorney fees — PLAUSIBLE, Spencer Fane], normalized by chemical, product category, noticing party, and penalty-vs-fees split, each record hyperlinked to its source PDF so the buyer can click and check; (2) OEHHA safe-harbor table — NSRLs/MADLs for ~300 chemicals [VERIFIED — fetched, free Excel export] cross-flagged against the full ~900-chemical list to expose the no-safe-harbor traps; (3) dossiers on the ~40 repeat private enforcers and their attorneys with historical settlement ranges; (4) 27 CCR Article 6 warning-content rules including the 2025 short-form amendment rendered as a deterministic per-channel label generator (on-product, website, Amazon listing, catalog). Assembly = parsing dozens of separate state publications and thousands of PDFs; clearly not an afternoon with ChatGPT.
why_prompt_cannot: The core value is the settlement benchmark data: real dollar amounts scattered across thousands of individual PDFs on the AG's server — a model will confidently hallucinate these numbers, and the buyer is pricing a $20-80k decision. Safe-harbor lookup across ~900 chemicals (only ~300 have levels) is exactly the long-document cross-referencing task where LLMs are measurably unreliable. And the warning text must be verbatim-correct per the amended Article 6 — a paraphrased warning is itself a fresh violation. Determinism plus assembled data beat a prompt in both directions here.
repeat_frequency: Per-notice. Enforcers serially target the same categories and retail channels — companies routinely receive multiple notices across years, and the label generator gets reused for every new SKU/channel — but honestly this is comparable-to-somewhat-better than DeckProof's per-event cadence, not per-shipment. The list itself replenishes at ~450/month.
weakest_link: The inbox is contested and lawyer-adjacent: plaintiff-side notices push buyers toward defense counsel, and Prop 65 defense firms already market off this same public list, so Sol's email must land in the days between letter-opening and counsel engagement, and the pitch must survive 'my lawyer handles that' (the honest answer: the kit is what makes the lawyer conversation 10x cheaper, or unnecessary for a boilerplate lead/phthalate notice). Free partial substitutes exist for the playbook layer only: the state's small-business 60-day-notice guide (p65warnings.ca.gov PDF) and the AG's raw searchable records — neither contains normalized benchmarks, enforcer dossiers, or the label generator, but they cap what the process-guide portion alone could charge.
evidence: https://oag.ca.gov/prop65/60-Day-Notice-Search-Results [VERIFIED — fetched, live data to 2026-08-06, free, CSV export]; https://oag.ca.gov/prop65 [VERIFIED — fetched; Annual Settlement Reports + notice search confirmed]; https://oehha.ca.gov/proposition-65/general-info/current-proposition-65-no-significant-risk-levels-nsrls-maximum [VERIFIED — fetched; ~300 chemicals, free Excel]; 2024 volume 5,398 notices [PLAUSIBLE — https://www.realestatelanduseandenvironmentallaw.com/prop-65-year-end-highlights-2024s-key-regulatory-changes-legal-battles-and-enforcement-trends.html]; monthly 358-539 notices [PLAUSIBLE — intertek.com insight bulletins]; 2023 settlements 797/$18.9M/88% fees [PLAUSIBLE — spencerfane.com]; competitor Prop65 Clearinghouse $1,150-1,800/yr law-firm data subscription, not a response kit [PLAUSIBLE — prop65clearinghouse.com/subscribe via search]; statutory $2,500/day/violation [PLAUSIBLE — multiple firm sources]; free state small-biz guide exists [VERIFIED URL surfaced: p65warnings.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2025-03/GuideSmallBusiness60day.pdf].

name: AbateProof — OSHA Citation Response and Abatement Documentation Kit (killed on T4)
one_line: PDF playbook + formulas spreadsheet + template pack for an employer that just received an OSHA citation: informal-conference penalty-reduction playbook, abatement-certification documents per 29 CFR 1903.19, and compliant written-program templates mapped to the most-cited standards.
buyer: Owner of a small US construction/manufacturing firm with no safety staff, holding a citation with a 15-working-day contest deadline and dated abatement deadlines.
trigger: Citation appears in OSHA's public enforcement database — named establishment, issuance date, penalty, standard cited. Data updated daily; federal citations visible ~5 days after employer receipt [PLAUSIBLE — osha.gov/help/establishment-search via search]. FY2024: 34,625 federal inspections, >$300M in citations [PLAUSIBLE — osha.gov/enforcement/2024-enforcement-summary via search snippet]; with state plans, plausibly 45-60k+ cited establishments/year [UNKNOWN — not directly counted].
trigger_url: https://www.osha.gov/ords/imis/establishment.html — NOT directly fetched; I fetched https://www.osha.gov/enforcement/toppenalties (HTTP 200, nav page confirming Data & Statistics Search exists) and enforcedata.dol.gov redirected to data.dol.gov without being followed. Freshness and field claims rest on OSHA's own help page via search [PLAUSIBLE].
list_size: Order of 45,000-60,000 cited establishments/year with dates and penalties, free [PLAUSIBLE for the federal 34,625-inspection component; state-plan share UNKNOWN]. Would beat DeckProof's list ~20x if it mattered — it does not, see displaces.
corpus: Would be: top ~500 most-cited 1910/1926 standards mapped to specific compliant abatement methods and documentation, FOM penalty-reduction rules (size/good-faith/quick-fix), sample written programs, abatement certification per 1903.19. Real but thinner than the Prop 65 corpus — much of it reconstructible from OSHA's own free publications.
why_prompt_cannot: Weaker claim than candidate 1: OSHA's Field Operations Manual and free employer-rights booklet are single coherent public documents a prompt can largely reproduce; the differentiated part (standard-to-abatement mapping) is real but moderate.
repeat_frequency: Per-citation; repeat inspections and failure-to-abate follow-ups are common, so genuinely recurring.
weakest_link: T4 KILL — an essentially identical product already ships to the identical buyer off the identical trigger: 'OSHA Citation Response System — 15 Days to Respond' at osha-defense.com/citation-defense, $447 one-time, 6 modules covering the 15-day response and informal conference [PLAUSIBLE — search snippet; direct fetch returned HTTP 503]. Additionally the buyer's inbox is already worked hard by safety consultants and defense attorneys who mine the same fresh-citation data, and OSHA's free 'Employer Rights and Responsibilities' booklet covers the process layer (T6 partial). Reported as a well-evidenced NO per instructions: excellent trigger arithmetic (fresh, daily, huge, penalty-anchored) but no displacement.

name: SEFA Forge — Single Audit Schedule Builder & Reconciler
one_line: A single local .html that turns a grantee's GL export and award list into an auditor-ready Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards: every ALN validated against the embedded SAM.gov assistance-listings database, cluster assignments applied from the OMB Compliance Supplement, Type A/B thresholds and 20%/40% major-program coverage computed per 2 CFR 200.518, the low-risk-auditee test run per 200.520, and every prior-year finding cross-referenced — before the auditor bills a single hour finding it.
buyer: Finance director / controller of a US nonprofit or small local government expending $1M+ in federal awards (single-audit-obligated), especially the tens of thousands whose PRIOR-YEAR audit — public on the FAC — already shows findings, a material weakness, or a late submission. Card purchase at $497 is inside a nonprofit finance director's signing authority; no procurement.
trigger: Two-tier, both from the same free federal database. Tier 1 (hot): the entity's latest single audit on the Federal Audit Clearinghouse shows findings — the API exposes is_repeat_finding and is_material_weakness flags per finding, plus auditee_name, EIN, fy_end_date, submitted_date, and even auditee_email. A repeat finding or material weakness costs them low-risk-auditee status, which by regulation DOUBLES required audit coverage from 20% to 40% of federal expenditures (2 CFR 200.518/200.520) — a forward, regulation-documented cost landing on their NEXT audit. Tier 2 (warm): every FAC filer's next deadline is computable from fy_end_date + 9 months (2 CFR 200.512, verified rule text) — a rolling, per-company, dated deadline every month of the year. A late FAC submission itself forfeits low-risk status for TWO subsequent years (200.520(a)(1)). ~40,000 single audits/year flow through the FAC (GAO-24-106173).
trigger_url: https://app.fac.gov/dissemination/search/ (fetched, HTTP 200, public) and https://www.fac.gov/api/ (fetched: free API, key requires only a valid email, PostgREST; api.fac.gov confirmed live by direct curl — returns API_KEY_MISSING without key, key is free). I did not complete the email signup, so I did not pull sample rows myself; field list verified via the published API dictionary at https://www.fac.gov/api/dictionary/ (fetched).
list_size: ~40,000 named entities/year with EIN, fiscal-year-end date, submission date, findings flags, and auditee email — free via FAC API (free key) and public CSV download [VERIFIED: GAO product page gao.gov/products/gao-24-106173 states ~40,000 single audits submitted in FY2023; fac.gov confirms public search + CSV + API]. Even post-2025 threshold rise to $1M, this is >10x DeckProof's ~2,400/year. The findings-flagged hot tier alone is plausibly 10,000+/year (GAO: $1.17T of $6.97T in 2017-21 awards tied to severe, recurring findings) [PLAUSIBLE on the tier split; the 40k total is VERIFIED].
corpus: The moat is assembled, not written: (1) the full active SAM.gov assistance-listings database (~2,300 ALNs with titles, agencies, cluster membership — free public API at open.gsa.gov/api/assistance-listings-api, refreshed each edition); (2) the cluster definitions and program matrices distilled from the ~2,200-page annual OMB Compliance Supplement (2025 edition released Nov 26, 2025) [VERIFIED via Grant Thornton/Feldesman summaries — PLAUSIBLE on exact page count]; (3) the 200.518 threshold cascade and 200.520 low-risk test encoded as deterministic checks with clause-level citations; (4) a library of the most common SEFA findings from FAC findings_text, mapped to the specific check that would have caught each. Rebuilding this means reading a 2,200-page document and a 2,300-row federal catalog — one-time work for Sol, annually refreshed, impossible to hold in a prompt.
why_prompt_cannot: An LLM hallucinates ALN titles and cluster membership (there are ~2,300, renumbered and retired continuously), and cannot reliably run the Type A/B threshold cascade plus percentage-of-coverage arithmetic across a real general-ledger export with hundreds of grant lines — exactly the cross-document reconciliation regime where models are measurably unreliable and being wrong creates a published federal audit finding. The buyer also cannot legally lean on their auditor to just do it: under GAGAS independence rules the SEFA is management's document, which is why every CPA-firm blog coaches auditees to prepare it themselves. And T8: the buyer needs no runtime, no LLM, no upload — one file:// .html.
repeat_frequency: Annual per entity — the audit recurs every fiscal year, the Compliance Supplement and ALN database change every year, so each edition is dated and the purchase recurs. Rolling deadlines (FYE + 9 months) mean sendable trigger volume every month, not seasonal spikes.
weakest_link: Willingness to pay: nonprofits are the cheapest buyers in B2B, and the whole-job partial substitute is 'let the auditor find it' — which costs billable hours and a public finding, but is the path of least resistance. Second shadow: SEFA generation is a named sub-feature of grant ERPs (AmpliFund advertises it; Sage Intacct supports it via custom fields) — this caps the upper end of the market, though the findings-flagged small entities in the hot tier are overwhelmingly QuickBooks shops, not AmpliFund customers. The dollar translation of losing low-risk status (extra major programs ≈ $10-15k+ in audit fees) is industry folklore, not a published number [PLAUSIBLE only] — the 20%→40% doubling itself is in regulation [VERIFIED].
evidence: VERIFIED https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.512 (fetched: 9-month deadline rule text; FAC packages public) | VERIFIED https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.520 (fetched: low-risk criteria incl. timely FAC submission 2 consecutive years, no material weaknesses, no repeat Type A findings) | VERIFIED https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.518 (fetched: 20% low-risk vs 40% coverage; Type A thresholds from $1M) | VERIFIED https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.339 (fetched: withhold payments, disallow costs, suspend/terminate award, debarment) | VERIFIED https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-24-106173 (fetched: ~40,000 single audits/yr to FAC in FY2023; $1.17T tied to severe recurring findings 2017-21) | VERIFIED https://www.fac.gov/api/ and https://www.fac.gov/api/dictionary/ (fetched: free key, endpoints general/findings/findings_text/federal_awards with auditee_email, is_repeat_finding, is_material_weakness, fy_end_date) | VERIFIED api.fac.gov live by direct curl (key-gated, key free) and https://app.fac.gov/dissemination/search/ HTTP 200 | PLAUSIBLE 2025 Compliance Supplement ~2,200 pages, released 2025-11-26 (grantthornton.com, feldesman.com summaries) | PLAUSIBLE single-audit threshold now $1M for FYs beginning on/after 2024-10-01 (multiple CPA sources) | VERIFIED no dedicated standalone SEFA-prep/validation product found in two targeted searches — only CPA-firm blog guidance, free state-auditor PDF guides (Ohio), and ERP sub-features | UNKNOWN exact count of FY2025 filings with findings flags (requires the free API key to compute precisely).

name: PackCheck UK — pEPR Data File Reconciler (honest verdict: does NOT displace)
one_line: A local .html that validates a UK producer's packaging-EPR data submission before it hits Defra's RPD portal — field and material-code checks against the published file spec, tonnage reconciliation against invoices, and a computed preview of the disposal-fee bill from published PackUK per-tonne rates so the producer sees the £ before certifying the data.
buyer: Compliance/finance manager at a UK 'large producer' under the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulations 2024 that reports its own data (no compliance scheme) — I counted 1,733 such direct registrants in today's register.
trigger: The Defra public register names every registered producer (with Companies House number, large/small flag, compliance-scheme field, and whether they owe disposal fees), and large producers face published recurring data-submission deadlines (April 1 / October 1) plus annual re-registration; disposal-fee invoices are computed directly from the data they submit at published per-tonne rates (plastic £423/t per House of Commons Library) — so a data error is real money on a real invoice, forward not sunk.
trigger_url: https://report-packaging-data.defra.gov.uk/public-register — fetched AND the CSV downloaded and parsed by me today (2026-08-06): 11,856 producer rows, 11,083 large, 773 small; 1,733 large producers list NO compliance scheme.
list_size: 11,083 named large producers with Companies House numbers, free CSV, updated daily [VERIFIED by my own download and row count today]. BUT the honestly addressable slice — large producers not delegating to a compliance scheme — is only ~1,733, refreshed annually, and it is a shared calendar deadline rather than per-company dated events.
corpus: Defra's RPD file specification and material/activity code tables, PackUK's published base-fee and RAM recyclability-modulation rate cards by year, and the reconciliation arithmetic — real assembly work, but an order of magnitude thinner than the Compliance Supplement corpus above.
why_prompt_cannot: Deterministic reconciliation of a multi-thousand-row packaging CSV against code tables and fee schedules is exactly what a prompt gets plausibly-but-wrongly; the fee preview must match PackUK's invoice to the pound. But the rules corpus itself is small enough that this moat is modest.
repeat_frequency: Twice yearly (April 1 / October 1 submissions) plus annual re-registration — genuinely recurring.
weakest_link: Three compounding kills against the displacement bar: (1) 84% of large producers (9,350 of 11,083) pay a compliance scheme (Wastepack, ERP UK, Clarity...) whose service includes checking and submitting the data — a whole-job substitute already under contract; (2) Defra's RPD portal performs its own upload validation on the file, so the free official tool covers the format layer, leaving only the fee-arithmetic layer; (3) the addressable direct-registrant list (~1,700, UK-only) is smaller than DeckProof's ~2,400/year, not bigger. Forward anchor and recurrence are real, but it loses on B and D and only ties on A — per the bar, that is not a displacement.
evidence: VERIFIED https://report-packaging-data.defra.gov.uk/public-register (fetched; CSV downloaded 2026-08-06, 11,856 rows counted: 11,083 L / 773 S / 1,733 L with no scheme — my own parse) | PLAUSIBLE plastic base fee £423/t, glass £192/t, PackUK confirmed 2025 fees 2025-06-27 (House of Commons Library briefing CBP-10352 and wastepackgroup.co.uk via search — not fetched directly) | PLAUSIBLE RPD upload validation exists (Defra RPS 330 guidance references data requirements; not tested) | UNKNOWN whether PackUK ships an official producer-facing fee calculator — if it does, the remaining value layer dies.

name: CitationProof — OSHA Penalty Audit & Informal Conference Pack
one_line: A self-contained local .html that recomputes every penalty item on a fresh OSHA citation against the published Field Operations Manual adjustment tables (and the buyer's state-plan equivalent), flags items assessed above the FOM-derived figure, runs the 15-working-day contest clock with federal holidays, and generates the informal-conference request letter, per-item negotiation sheets, petition-for-modification-of-abatement and abatement-certification documents.
buyer: Owner or safety manager of a US small/mid-size employer (construction, manufacturing, warehousing, roofing) whose site just had an OSHA inspection opened — the person who will personally sit in the informal conference and can put $497 on a company card without procurement.
trigger: The employer's name and inspection-open date appear in OSHA's free public establishment search within days of the inspection (page states data current through 08/04/2026 on an 08/06 fetch). Citations follow weeks later carrying penalties up to $16,550 per serious violation / $165,514 willful-repeat (effective 15-Jan-2026) and a hard 15-working-day contest deadline; informal conferences average ~49% penalty reduction. Sol emails at inspection-open: 'your citation is coming — be ready before the clock starts.' US-only buyers, so CAN-SPAM opt-out applies. Unlike ECRM, this is US-government public-domain data with no anti-scraping terms.
trigger_url: https://www.osha.gov/ords/imis/establishment.html [VERIFIED, free, no login, data through 08/04/2026]. Record-level proof by live query: https://www.osha.gov/ords/imis/establishment.search?p_logger=1&establishment=roofing&State=TX&officetype=all&Office=all&sitezip=&p_case=all&p_violations_exist=all&startmonth=01&startday=01&startyear=2026&endmonth=08&endday=06&endyear=2026 returned 20 named, dated records (e.g. 'Collins Roofing Inc.', inspection 03/11/2026, NAICS 238160, TX) [VERIFIED by direct fetch].
list_size: 30,273 federal inspections FY2025 (34,625 FY2024) [VERIFIED — https://www.osha.gov/enforcement/current-enforcement-summary]. The same free search covers the 20+ state plans too ('Fed & State' filter verified in the form HTML), so total named/dated establishments plausibly ~55-70k/yr [PLAUSIBLE for the state-plan share]. Even federal-only is ~12x ECRM's 2,400/yr. Every record is free, named, dated, with NAICS and state for segmentation.
corpus: One-time heavy assembly: (1) FOM Chapter 6 gravity-based penalty tables plus size (up to 70%), good-faith (25%), history and quick-fix reduction schedules, every figure cited to its FOM paragraph; (2) the divergent penalty schedules and appeal deadlines of all state plans — Cal/OSHA, Oregon, Washington, Michigan differ materially from federal; (3) a federal-holiday-aware 15-working-day and abatement-date calculator; (4) a mined dataset from OSHA's own public enforcement records comparing initial vs current (settled) penalty by state and NAICS, so the buyer sees the realistic reduction to ask for. Items 2 and 4 are the moat — real work a prompt cannot hold.
why_prompt_cannot: A prompt drafts a plausible-sounding conference letter, but cannot reliably hold 20+ state penalty schedules plus FOM adjustment arithmetic, and does not contain the initial-vs-settled penalty dataset at all. The arithmetic is deterministic and being wrong is expensive: a mis-computed contest date makes the citation an unappealable final order, and failure-to-abate runs $16,550/day. Buyer self-verifies every output figure against the cited public FOM table and https://www.osha.gov/penalties — the artefact carries its own authority; no credential needed.
repeat_frequency: Per-inspection. Multi-site and high-hazard-NAICS employers are re-inspected routinely, and a first citation raises repeat exposure (repeat = $165,514/violation), making a second purchase more likely, not less. At parity with or slightly better than DeckProof's per-event cadence; not T7 buy-once-ever.
weakest_link: Timing squeeze: the citation may issue weeks after the inspection becomes visible, and the 15-working-day clock starts at citation receipt — so Sol sells at inspection-open ('prepare before it lands'), a softer moment than deadline-in-hand. A $447 checklist-style rival exists (osha-defense.com 'Citation Response System', 6 modules, documents/templates only, no penalty recomputation) [PLAUSIBLE — seen in search results; site unreachable at fetch time, SSL error] — it validates the price point but crowds the slot; differentiation is the deterministic penalty engine + state-plan corpus. Also OSHA inspections fell ~20% Apr-Sep 2025 and inspector headcount is down 846→736 [PLAUSIBLE — Haynes Boone alert], shrinking the stream.

name: NoticeProof UK — HSE Improvement Notice Compliance Pack
one_line: PDF system plus formulas-only spreadsheet for UK employers served an HSE improvement notice: compliance-by-date planner, extension-request letters, evidence-of-compliance templates, and escalation-cost arithmetic (unlimited fines / prosecution for non-compliance).
buyer: Director or H&S lead of a UK SME named on the HSE public register of enforcement notices with a compliance-by date approaching. UK corporate subscribers, so PECR-workable outbound.
trigger: Company name published on the HSE public register of enforcement notices with issue date and compliance deadline; non-compliance with an improvement notice is a criminal offence with unlimited fines.
trigger_url: https://resources.hse.gov.uk/notices/ — register root fetched HTTP 200, title 'Public register of enforcement notices' with search-the-database link [VERIFIED]; the deep list pages returned HTTP 500 during this scan, so record-level enumeration is UNVERIFIED today.
list_size: UNKNOWN by direct fetch (list pages 500'd). HSE annual statistics indicate roughly 7,000 notices/yr [PLAUSIBLE, secondary sources] — bigger than ECRM's 2,400 but far smaller than the OSHA stream.

name: ADV-Check
one_line: A single local .html that cross-checks an RIA's Form ADV Part 1A (structured data) against its Part 2A brochure PDF and Form CRS before the 90-day annual updating amendment deadline, flagging every inconsistency the SEC's examiners are documented to look for (RAUM mismatch, custody answers, fee schedules, disciplinary disclosures), each finding shown side-by-side with the two source passages.
buyer: The Chief Compliance Officer of a small/mid SEC- or state-registered investment adviser (at firms under ~$1B AUM the CCO is typically an owner-principal with a corporate card; they already buy compliance manuals and webinars at $500-900 self-serve). US buyers, CAN-SPAM opt-out email is legal.
trigger: Every registered adviser must file an annual updating amendment within 90 days of its fiscal year end (Advisers Act Rule 204-1) — a dated, per-firm, recurring deadline. The SEC publishes the full roster monthly as a free CSV including each firm's name, website, state, RAUM items, and Latest ADV Filing Date (the filing anniversary predicts next year's deadline; 8,179 of 17,018 firms filed in March, i.e., Dec-FYE firms facing a March 31 deadline every year). Sharper still: Part 2A brochures are also published free as monthly bulk PDFs, so Sol can pre-run the check on a target and open the email with the firm's own live discrepancy ('your Part 1 Item 5.F reports $412M RAUM; your current brochure Item 4 says $353M').

corpus: An item-by-item crosswalk of every Form ADV Part 1A item to its corresponding Part 2A brochure item and Form CRS line (~60-80 deterministic checks: Item 5.F RAUM vs brochure Item 4, custody Items 9.A/9.B vs Item 15, fee items 5.E vs Item 5, disciplinary Item 11 vs Item 9, compensation-for-referrals 8.H vs Item 14, wrap-fee 5.I vs Appendix 1, client types 5.D vs Item 7, plus date/arithmetic/staleness checks), fused with a deficiency taxonomy assembled from SEC risk alerts and enforcement orders. Authoring = weeks of reading the ADV instructions, risk alerts, and settled orders, plus in-page PDF text extraction (inlined pdf.js) and a parser for the buyer's own IAPD data. A one-time ~$300 review session with a former examiner or RIA compliance consultant validates the checklist — a line item, not a dependency; the output needs no authority because every finding is two quoted passages that disagree.
why_prompt_cannot: Honestly: both documents are public, so a CCO can paste them into a chatbot and get a plausible partial answer — that is the real competitive floor. What the prompt does not hold: the complete item-by-item crosswalk (an LLM flags the mismatches it happens to notice; an exam deficiency comes from the one it missed), reliable arithmetic and cross-referencing across a 50-100 page brochure plus a 171-field structured filing, and deterministic repeatability the CCO can put in the compliance file as evidence of review. The product ingests the structured Part 1 data exactly, checks 100% of mapped items every time, and cites both source passages for each finding.
repeat_frequency: Annual per firm (Rule 204-1 annual updating amendment), plus other-than-annual amendments on material changes during the year — a genuinely recurring, dated purchase occasion, and the buyer re-runs it before every filing.
weakest_link: The prompt floor: because the inputs are public (no MNPI barrier), a diligent CCO with ChatGPT gets a decent free approximation, so willingness to pay $650 rests on completeness/determinism — settled only by a live test. Second: roughly a third of small RIAs outsource the annual amendment to compliance consultants or platforms (COMPLY, SmartRIA, RIA in a Box) where the review is bundled, shrinking the self-filing segment. Third: revenue is seasonal — 48% of firms hit their deadline in March, so Jan-Mar carries a disproportionate share of the year.

name: PressProof
one_line: A single local .html an issuer's controller opens on their own machine the night before earnings: it loads the draft press release plus the prior 10-Q/10-K XBRL facts via file picker and deterministically recomputes every figure — cross-foots all tables, ties EPS to net income and share counts, ties non-GAAP reconciliations (including the tax-effect line that burned Planet Labs), checks YoY deltas and prior-period figures against what was actually filed — with nothing leaving the machine, because unreleased earnings are MNPI and cannot legally-safely be pasted into a chatbot.
buyer: Controller or VP Finance at a micro/small-cap US public company (roughly the 4,000+ 10-Q filers below the Workiva tier, where the earnings release is authored in Word/Excel and tied out by hand at midnight). $750 is under any corporate-card threshold; the buyer personally owns the embarrassment if a corrected release goes out.
trigger: Quarterly earnings, visible and dated for every company: each filer's 10-Q deadline is computable (40/45 days after quarter end by filer category), last quarter's filing date predicts this quarter's within days, and companies announce their earnings date in advance. EDGAR publishes it all free. Outreach lands in the 2-3 weeks before each company's known reporting date, four times a year per company.
trigger_url: [VERIFIED, fetched and parsed] https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/full-index/2026/QTR2/form.idx — 5,408 unique companies filed a 10-Q in Q2 2026 alone (5,400 filed 8-Ks). Free, no login, updated continuously.
list_size: [VERIFIED by direct fetch+count] 5,408 unique 10-Q filers in a single quarter, i.e., ~21,000+ named, dated filing events per year; company names/CIK/addresses free on EDGAR, domains resolvable from company IR pages ([VERIFIED] 10,398 entries in https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json, fetched). Roughly 9x DeckProof's ~2,400 dated events/year even after cutting the Workiva-tier large caps.
corpus: A tie-out check library reverse-engineered from real correction 8-Ks and comment letters — a taxonomy of what actually goes wrong (non-GAAP tax-effect errors, EPS share-count mismatches, transposed prior-year columns, cross-foot failures, guidance mis-statements), plus an inlined XBRL/iXBRL parser so the prior filed 10-Q loads as authoritative facts, plus inlined docx/PDF text extraction — all in one classic-script file:// page. Assembling the error taxonomy means reading hundreds of correction 8-Ks and 10-Q/As on EDGAR: real one-time work, exactly the thick-corpus moat, and the output is pure arithmetic the buyer verifies in seconds.
why_prompt_cannot: The block is policy before capability: a draft earnings release is material nonpublic information, and under SOX 302 disclosure controls a controller cannot defensibly paste it into ChatGPT — so the free substitute is off the table at precisely the moment of need. Second, LLM arithmetic across multi-table financial documents is measurably unreliable, and this is a domain where one wrong recomputed number is worse than none; deterministic recomputation with a check-by-check log is the product.
repeat_frequency: Quarterly per company (4 releases/year plus 10-K season) — genuinely per-filing, the highest natural cadence of any candidate examined.
weakest_link: Adjacent funded competition: Workiva already sells number-consistency to large caps, and DataSnipper and Suralink (launched its AI tie-out Apr 2026 — VERIFIED https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260408180770/en/) are productizing tie-out for audit firms; an issuer-side press-release checker is a plausible feature release for any of them. Second, the anchor is probabilistic — a corrected 8-K is a real, public, stock-moving embarrassment, but no statute attaches a dated fine to it. Third, public-company finance staff are the most vendor-cautious cohort in this exercise; the local-only/nothing-uploaded architecture is the answer, but it must be believed from a cold email.
